To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRAP binds to multiple receptors on hepatocyte surface and the adhesive domain of TRAP is a promising vaccine antigen.
we have produced recombinant ECD (extracelluar domain) and A domains of TRAP (thombospondin-related anonymous proteins) and demonstrated their adhesive properties.
we have developed procedures for the recombinant production and purification of the entire TRAP ECD and A-domain, which we have shown to bind to HepG2 hepatocytes in a dose-dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular determinants of the TRAP protein that mediate the interaction with host cell receptors and thus play a role in hepatocyte infection.
the development of recombinant proteins for the study of malaria parasite invasion and for vaccine development.
the development of recombinant TRAPS (thrombosponsin-related anonymous proteins) and their functional analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the A domain and ECD bind to hepatocytes, but not to sulphated lipids.
TRAP EDC and the A domain are both adhesive proteins that bind heparin and interact with hepatocyte receptors.
the ECD and A domains of TRAP are adhesive proteins that are capable of binding to HepG2 and possibly other cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TRAP A domain and the ECD have the ability to bind to hepatocyte receptors and that these binding activities are not inhibited by sulphatide analogs.
the TRAP A domain has two ligand-binding sites and the TRAP ECD binds with a higher affinity to heparin than the A domain.
we have developed procedures for the recombinant production and characterization of TRAP ECD and A domains and have shown that they are functional adhesive domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRAP is a multi-domain protein and the A-domain is not a single binding site but a multi-binding domain.

the ECD of TRAP is a bivalent cation-dependent adhesive protein that can bind to multiple receptors on hepatocytes, and the A domain is an adhesive module with a higher affinity for hepan sulphate proteoglycans than for sulphatide.
the ECD and the TRAP A domain are monomeric, non-aggregated proteins that bind specifically to HepG2 cell membranes.
